thread.title: Rebound Predicted For Singapore Stock Market

author: rttnews.com
title: Rebound Predicted For Singapore Stock Market
text:
Rebound Predicted For Singapore Stock Market 9/27/2018 8:00 PM ET
The Singapore stock market on Thursday ended the six-day winning streak in which it had advanced more than 100 points or 3.1 percent. The Straits Times Index now rests just above the 3,235-point plateau although it may bounce higher again on Friday.
The global forecast for the Asian markets is firm, with support expected from the oil and technology stocks. The European and U.S. markets were up and the Asian bourses are tipped to follow suit.
The STI finished slightly lower on Thursday as losses from the financials and properties were offset by gains from the industrials and plantations.
For the day, the index eased 2.84 points or 0.09 percent to finish at 3,236.26 after trading between 3,232.21 and 3,263.08. Volume was 1.2 billion shares worth 1.01 billion Singapore dollars. There were 201 decliners and 188 gainers.
Among the actives, Golden Agri-Resources surged 2.08 percent, while Genting Singapore plunged 1.89 percent, CapitaLand Commercial Trust and Yangzijiang Shipbuilding both soared 1.71 percent, Thai Beverage spiked 1.46 percent, Wilmar International jumped 1.27 percent, United Overseas Bank tumbled 1.20 percent, CapitaLand skidded 0.88 percent, Comfort DelGro climbed 0.84 percent, SembCorp Industries advanced 0.65 percent, SingTel added 0.63 percent, DBS Group collected 0.43 percent, Ascendas REIT shed 0.38 percent, Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation lost 0.26 percent and Hutchison Port Holdings, Singapore Press Holdings and Keppel Corporation were unchanged,
The lead from Wall Street is upbeat as stocks opened higher on Thursday. They faded slightly in the afternoon but still finished firmly in the green.
The Dow added 54.65 points or 0.21 percent to 26,439.93, while the NASDAQ gained 51.60 points or 0.65 percent to 8,041.97 and the S&P was up 8.03 points or 0.28 percent to 2,914.00.
A notable advance by shares of Apple (AAPL) contributed to the higher close on Wall Street after J.P. Morgan initiated coverage of the company's stock with an Overweight rating.
In economic news, the Commerce Department noted a bigger than expected jump in durable goods orders in August. The Commerce Department also said the pace of U.S. economic growth in the second quarter was unrevised at 4.2 percent from the previous estimate.
Also, the Labor Department noted a rebound in initial jobless claims in the week ended September 22. And the National Association of Realtors said pending home sales dropped much more than expected in August.
Crude oil prices moved higher on Thursday, amid concerns that sanctions on Iran from November may result in supply shortage in the market. Crude oil futures for November delivery ended up $0.55 or 0.8 percent at $72.12 a barrel.
Closer to home, Singapore will provide August figures for producer prices later today; in July, prices were up 1.7 percent on month and 10.9 percent on year.
